experiments.name: cost_breakeven
experiments.question: How high can the all-in round turn go before the best thing the search has found stops paying?
experiments.verdict: the best cell of 262,655 pays +47.490 round trips over 2,695 trades, which breaks even at an all-in round turn of $29.09 on MNQ (the search charged $0.60). after shrinking for the winner's curse it breaks even at $0.60. the 99th percentile of ALL 262,655 cells breaks even at $0.61 and the median at $-0.01, so the winner's headroom over the modelled cost is 2521.60x what the 99th percentile of the pile gets for free. at 258 trades a week it is worth the ladder in the report; the practical reading is that anything above $29.09 a round turn makes this a losing system no matter how it is executed

experiments.name: session_split
experiments.question: Is the overnight session different enough from RTH that searching and pricing them together is wrong?
experiments.verdict: overnight moves are 0.69x RTH in dispersion (a random split of the same sizes gives 1.02x, so the session effect is 15x what splitting nothing produces) overnight bars are 0.45x the RTH range, which says nothing about cost -- a quiet market can still be expensive to cross MEASURED on NQ top-of-book: spread is 3.0 ticks in RTH and 5.0 overnight (1.67x wider), against a cost model that charges 1 tick for both -- overnight results ARE optimistic, and 70% of the tier-1 tape is overnight
